name: The A-Series and B-Series of Time

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ralph Shain argues forward and backward time travel are categorically different: relativistic time dilation is conceptually harmless (in Boulle's novel Merou could not return to Soror for a thousand years), but Escape from the Planet of the Apes' backward jump is conceptually impossible because it treats the open future as fixed like the past - Hasslein's plan to kill baby Milo is the Grandfather Paradox, checked against presentist, possibilist, and eternalist ontologies of time. The real philosophical engine is Aristotle's sea-battle argument from the law of excluded middle: since Cornelius's story of the takeover is past for the apes and future for 1973 humans, the film's causal loop (Milo saved at the circus) enacts the fatalist conclusion that the ape takeover will necessarily occur. Hasslein's freeway image of time defeats itself - switching lanes means landing in the past of a different, parallel universe, so the apes' jump would be travel between worlds, not times.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: Tomorrow Is Yesterday
samples.relation: Uses the Bajoran Prophets, who experience no linear time ('What is this... time?'), to frame a tour of time's metaphysics: Newton's absolute container versus Leibniz's relationism (the incoherence of a 'temporal vacuum'), Augustine's mind-dependent time (illustrated by 'The Inner Light' and O'Brien's implanted prison years in 'Hard Time'), and McTaggart's argument that neither the A-series nor the B-series can account for change, illustrated by Tasha Yar's death in 'Skin of Evil' and Kirk's Liar-paradox victories over Nomad and Norman. The chapter defends the A-series via tense, then weighs presentism — which would make 'Tomorrow Is Yesterday' and 'Trials and Tribble-ations' impossible — against eternalism, whose fatalism Data embraces when his severed head turns up in 'Time's Arrow' ('It has occurred. It will occur.'), and which finally makes sense of prophets who see the future in 'Destiny.'

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 6. Nebula’s Time Travel Paradox
samples.relation: Charlene Esby defends Endgame against the charge that Nebula killing her past self is a plot hole. She reconstructs the grandfather paradox from Nathaniel Schachner's 'Ancestral Voices,' explains how conceiving time as a fourth dimension makes travel conceivable, and deploys Aristotle's Physics (time as the number of change and rest) and the De Interpretatione sea-battle problem, where the past is necessary but the future contingent on present choices, to argue the Avengers' victory depends on free choices made now, which is why the Ancient One releases the Time Stone only on Banner's promise. The resolution is Hulk's subjective-timeline point: once traveled to, the past becomes the traveler's present, so present Nebula kills past Nebula in a shared present rather than negating her own future, just as Thanos from the past arrives alive in a present where he already died.

samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: Through a hot-tub dialogue in Prismo's Time Room, the chapter walks Jake through the main theories of time: McTaggart's A-theory versus B-theory, plus presentism, the growing block, eternalism and four-dimensionalism, illustrated with the mirror-Finn dream, Farmworld Finn, Jake's unchangeable croak dream, and the Ancient Psychic Tandem War Elephant as a thing stretched across past, present and future selves. Booko's description of the multiverse becomes a springboard for David Lewis's possible-worlds realism and Everett's many-worlds reading of Prismo's 'alternate wish worlds'. Finally, quotes from McTaggart and Bergson delivered as Finn's Glasses of Nerdicon rant argue that time resists spatial and scientific analysis and must be lived, which the authors tie to relativity, black-hole cosmology and Prismo's Time Room as the one dimension outside time.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 7. Doctor Who as Philosophy Four-Dimensionalism and Time Travel
samples.relation: Decker asks what the universe must be like if Doctor Who's time travel were real, using David Lewis's distinction between personal and external time and the TARDIS as a Wellsian (not Thornian) time machine traversing a 'hypertime' vortex. After surveying the arrows of time and paradoxes like the bootstrap paradox ('Day of the Daleks') and the grandfather paradox (imagined via Tegan's grandfather), and rejecting Deutsch-Lockwood's Many-Worlds and growing-block solutions, he argues the Whoniverse fits 'Four-Dimensional Realism'/eternalism, quoting the Twelfth Doctor that time's passage is an illusion of 'still pictures.' He then confronts 4DR's threat to free will and moral responsibility, finding compatibilism and 'fixed points' inadequate given eternalism's succession-not-production of events.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Miller reconciles Kyle's 'no fate but what we make' with Sarah's 'you're dead already': eternalism (defended by the special-relativity argument Hilary Putnam made famous) makes 2029 as real as 1994, so Judgment Day cannot be changed, and the grandfather paradox - using Caesar's unalterable assassination as the model - blocks the T-101 from preventing its own existence. She then tests growing-block, presentist, meta-time, and branching-timeline (McCall-style) models against T2 and T3, asking whether any lets Sarah's attack on Cyberdyne legitimately delay Judgment Day. The conclusion works under every model: even on a fixed four-dimensional block, Judgment Day happens because of what humans do, not independently of them, so fixed fate and making our own future turn out to be compatible.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Davies defends Lost's convoluted plotting using Aristotle's Poetics, arguing the show works as a tragicomic epic that keeps closure and relevance even with Juliet's pre-crash storyline, genre mixing (Hurley's golf course beside Sayid's captivity), and shifting characters like Ben. He then uses the 'We have to go back' flash-forward to lay out McTaggart's two conceptions of time, eternalism versus presentism, and argues the flash-forward pushes viewers toward fatalism about Jack's already-fixed meeting with Kate near LAX. Finally he contends the past cannot be changed - Hurley in 2007 cannot undo his 1977 stay in the Dharma Initiative, since contradictions would entail everything - so viewers enjoy the time-travel plot by 'shielding' its mutually contradictory time lines.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: The End
samples.relation: Berghofer uses the Rebels episode 'A World Between Worlds' to ask whether Ezra changed the past when he pulled Ahsoka out of her duel with Vader, arguing that past-changing time travel breeds contradiction: the grandfather paradox looms over his attempt to save Kanan ('if he is taken out of this moment, you all die'), and on the Lewis-style consistent model Ezra caused but never changed the past. He surveys presentism, eternalism, and the growing block to locate Star Wars' metaphysics of time — Ezra's travel rules out presentism, and the Mortis god's 'the future, by its nature, can be changed' fits a growing block with an open future. Anakin's tragedy of acting to prevent prophesied events and thereby causing them frames the whole analysis.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
samples.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
samples.relation: Dinello maps Westworld point-by-point onto Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism: the park is a concentration camp that kills the juridical person (hosts as chattel in a 'fictitious world' of Western propaganda), the moral person (Ford forcing Bernard to murder Theresa, Maeve's engineered failure to protect her daughter), and individuality itself (surveillance, resets, 'ghastly marionettes'), with Ford as a Mengele-like ideological scientist who, like Hitler, merely plagiarizes popular myths (John Ford's Westerns, R.U.R.). Liberation then follows Fanon's Wretched of the Earth: violence as a 'cleansing force' that frees the colonized mind, so Maeve's suicide-by-incineration (echoing Plath's Lady Lazarus) and Dolores's beating of the Man in Black and massacre of the Delos board enact decolonization as the creation of 'new men' - a new Robo sapiens species - with Sartre's endorsement that killing eliminates oppressor and oppressed in one go, while Fanon's warning that hatred and revenge are not an agenda sets the conditions for what the resistance must do next.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 24. Post-Factual Democracy
samples.relation: Hendricks and Vestergaard open with Trump's inauguration lies and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' to define post-factual democracy: a state in which opportune political narratives replace facts and evidence as the basis of debate, opinion formation and policymaking. Unlike Machiavelli, who taught that lies must at least be concealed, the post-factual politician pays no price for exposed falsehood once social media, the attention economy and populist us-versus-them narratives engineered for indignation and fear have stripped journalists and fact-checkers of authority — Arendt's remark that mass leaders show 'extreme contempt for facts as such' before fitting reality to their lies. Using Habermas's deliberative model and even minimal accountability theories of voting, they argue post-factuality destroys democratic legitimacy, and defend a 'factual democracy' that trusts science and journalism without becoming a technocracy — the real-world echo of the Party's command to reject the evidence of your eyes.

samples.book: 103 - David Bowie and Philosophy - Rebel Rebel
samples.title: 7. David Bowie, Political Philosopher
samples.relation: Hill reconstructs Bowie's political odyssey as a working-out of what freedom and oppression are: 'Cygnet Committee' repudiates revolution powered by resentment (echoing Nietzsche on socialism's despotic annihilation of the individual), 'Big Brother' and Diamond Dogs diagnose the crowd's flight from freedom into leadership, and the Nietzschean self-as-artwork - 'give style to one's character,' the 'mortal with potential of a superman' - curdles into the Thin White Duke's 'rock stars are fascists' collapse of celebrity into totalitarian leadership. The Berlin Trilogy then turns the critique inward: 'Heroes'' ironic lovers unmask romantic anti-totalitarianism (either side of the Antifaschistischer Schutzwall), 'Neuköln' discovers immigrants' mere survival, and Lodger's 'Fantastic Voyage' lands on structural, Marxist questions of how 'we' are to become free.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: “I Want to Conquer the World”
samples.relation: Uses Agamben's bios/zoē distinction (with Foucault on biopolitics and fragmented sovereignty, Hardt and Negri's 'Empire', Marx on surplus-value, and Rosa Luxemburg on unchecked capital) to read the Anderson Station massacre, Murtry shooting Coop on New Terra, and Protogen infecting 1.5 million Belters on Eros as reductions of Belter life to bare life that corporate sovereigns may kill without homicide. It then argues the instability capitalism creates births authoritarian sovereigns — Murtry's martial law, Inaros's Free Navy, Duarte's Laconia — whose followers (Chandra Wei, Cyn, Santiago Singh) display the 'total, unrestricted, unconditional loyalty' Arendt says totalitarian power demands, and closes with Foucault's warning that liberal government's security-for-freedom trade slides into the very corruption and oppression it was meant to prevent.

samples.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
samples.title: 3. Gestational Totalitarianism
samples.relation: Kolb reads Gilead through Arendt's The Human Condition and The Origins of Totalitarianism: when reproduction becomes the means of production, women's labor is targeted, forcing fertile women into Animal laborans status as 'national resources' while denying them the creative freedom of Homo faber. She traces the polis/oikos split from Aristotle through Puritan capitalism to show Gilead overcorrecting into Aunt Lydia's 'freedom from'—totalitarian control of birth legitimized by the Rachel and Bilhah story and a Pauline creation story. The chapter ends with the transitional generation's forgetting (Offred's cave-delusion with Nick evoking Plato's Allegory of the Cave, the Holocaust documentarian 'thinking about how not to think') and Ofglen's bomb, arguing that thoughtfulness and literacy, not violence, are the only hopes against totalitarianism.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 10 Understanding the Reigns of T’Challa and Killmonger through Hannah Arendt
samples.relation: Sinanan reads both reigns through Arendt's account of collective responsibility: T'Challa moves from conscience-based 'I am not king of all people' to owning what Wakanda did in its name ('He was the truth I chose to omit') and finally to political action in Oakland and at the UN, while Killmonger — an MIT-educated Navy SEAL embodying the collective that formed him — becomes the imperialist he opposed, his 'burn it all' revolution matching Arendt's warning about totalitarian domination from within. She compares Killmonger's council speech and herb-burning directly to Hitler's 1924 Munich trial speech, reads his manipulation of the challenge ritual as totalitarian propaganda that organizes rather than persuades, and credits Nakia, Okoye, Shuri, and Ramonda with refusing Arendt's ultimate danger, indifference.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 9. What Fuckin’ Chance Does a Kid Have
samples.relation: Joseph Westfall argues that Louis's parent-hating bits - the baby he doesn't know who 'might fuckin' hate Jews,' the four-year-old 'asshole,' 'I love her, but I wish she was never born' - voice the real ambivalence of parenthood while showing that children are developmentally incapable of responsibility, so parents must not blame kids for being kids. He contrasts Louis's unknowable, selfish infant with Augustine's doctrine that unbaptized babies are simply evil, and reads Louis's parenting maxim - 'you're not raising the kid in front of you, you're raising the grownup they're going to be' - through childhood as a state of becoming: Jizzanthapuss is on the road to Hitler thanks to his weak mother, and Louie berating little Jane realizes 'I'm her first asshole,' shaping the men she will later attract. Good parenting is keeping kids alive plus forming the future adult, which is why Louis denies his daughters cell phones (they prevent learning empathy face-to-face) and puts his daughter on the smelly city bus while his Mercedes waits.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 6. The Psychiatrist as Sociopathic God
samples.relation: Hassert takes Lecter's 'First principles, Clarice' at its Aristotelian word - nature is revealed through capacities and action, as an acorn's telos is not pumpkins and a kitten will never be a Great Dane - to explain Lecter's psychiatry: he reads each patient's essence and potential, prescribing Mason Verger's face-peeling so appearance finally matches essence, and force-raising Will toward equality so that Aristotelian perfect friendship between the alike-in-virtue (which Franklyn's flattery can never reach) might become possible. Reading God through Augustine's account of evil as the destruction of a preexisting good and Mischa's murder, the chapter argues that Lecter emulates a capricious deity - 'Typhoid and swans - it all comes from the same place' - and, unlike Nietzsche, does not pronounce God dead but merely misconceptualized, while his friendships fail because he must corrupt the other into his own image rather than love an equal.

samples.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
samples.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
samples.relation: Foresman and Tobienne deploy Aristotle's apparatus of essence and accident, the ten categories, and actuality versus potentiality to define the monster and explain the show's appeal. They test candidates against canon: whether hunting is essential or accidental to Sam after Azazel's kills, what John Winchester in 'Dead Man's Blood' treats as essential to vampire substance, and Madison's transformation in 'Heart' from actual human and potential werewolf into actual monster, concluding that monstrosity lies in thought and action rather than appearance, as the human-hunting but human Benders confirm. Tracing 'monster' to the Latin monstrum, a sign or omen, they argue monsters are monsters only through their relation to human self-importance, so our 'speciesist' prejudice is exactly why we love watching them hunted, and why we love Supernatural.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greeley argues the zombie embodies a specifically modern fear of losing our humanity: walkers are persons stripped of the potential Aristotle and Aquinas made the measure of human worth, which is why Rick uniquely eulogizes the walkers he puts down ('I'm sorry this happened to you'). Following Aries, he traces modern death anxiety to the split of faith from reason and reads the CDC arc ('TS-19') as science offering only a self-destruct quick death where Jacqui's 'wrath of God' guess at least offers meaning. Rousseau's claim that civilization corrupts explains the survivors' return to the woods, where pizza-deliverer Glenn's heroics and the 'kingpin' Guillermo protecting nursing-home patients show the apocalypse can bring out the best in us while the Bradbury's Sale storefront and trampled Walmart worker hint we were already the walking dead.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nys uses Brent's quiz grievance about Mr. Spock (half-Vulcan, half-human) and his Crufts pedigree-dog analogy, Gareth's 'look at the ears' classification test, the dwarf/midget/elf/pixie interrogation of Alex, and Tim and Dawn's 'lethal blow' prank to introduce the problem of natural kinds. Realist answers come from Kripke (water is H2O whatever we call it), Aristotle's matter-and-form essences, and the DNA evidence separating Bornean clouded leopards from mainland cousins, while Wittgenstein's language games and Quine's point that our innate similarity senses mislead support the constructivist that we lay classification on an unstructured world. The verdict: nature supplies real differences but never carves itself into kinds, and the line-drawing remains up to us.

samples.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
samples.title: Where Do We Go from Here
samples.relation: Argues on Aristotelian–Thomist grounds that WALL-E and EVE cannot truly be intelligent: they are artificial because their formal cause lies outside them in the Buy n Large engineers' minds, whereas natural things like the captain, the cockroach, and the plant have intrinsic formal causes. Intelligence is the act of an intellectual soul — the formal cause of a living thing — so machines at best mimic WALL-E's grasp of spoon-ness, fork-ness, and spork-ness, as Kreeft's comparison of a computer to a library building that does not understand its books makes clear. The conclusion is that AI is qualitatively, not merely technologically, impossible, and Pixar's live-action cinematography is precisely what tricks us into taking the robots as real.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Aftermath of Tragedy
samples.relation: Argues that Grave of the Fireflies works as a critique of anime's child-hero convention: Seita acts exactly like a plucky anime protagonist when he defies his not-actually-evil aunt, strikes out on his own with Setsuko, ignores the farmer's advice to apologize and return, and demands a quick fix from the doctor — but these 'heroic' choices kill them both, because he lacks the developed capacity to reason. Against the medieval 'child as little adult' picture that most anime (Dragon Ball, Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!) romanticizes, the chapter deploys Aristotle's view of children as unfinished beings who cannot yet reason or achieve happiness, concluding the film is a cautionary tale about the years of nurture and guidance real children need.

samples.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
samples.title: 5. Other People’s Body Parts
samples.relation: Explains Kyle Spencer's horror at the body Madison and Zoe assembled from other people's parts through the history of soul-body theories: Aristotle's De Anima account of the soul as the faculties of a living body (plus the Physiognomonics claim that small people have small minds - poor Ma Petite), Plato's Timaeus on body parts designed for philosophy and reincarnation into bodies fitted to one's vices, Avicenna's soul as a faculty-binding nexus that chooses its bodily vehicle like a vehicle serves its owner, and Merleau-Ponty's habitual body (the Axeman's axe as part of his body, phantom limbs), which best explains why walking around on someone else's legs 'has got to mess with you a little'.

name: The Best of All Possible Worlds

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Is Monk’s Certainty Justified
samples.relation: Rauhut tests Monk's method against two models of discovery: Holmes-style eliminatism, modeled on Popper's falsification via reductio ad absurdum, and CSI-style confirmationism in the mold of Hempel and Carnap (Gil Grissom letting evidence speak). Monk fits neither — in 'Mr. Monk and the Astronaut' he refuses to eliminate the alibi-solid Steve Wagner, and in 'Mr. Monk Falls in Love' he ignores a hatpin, a motive, and a confession pointing at Leyla. Instead Monk is an 'epiphanist': he registers every anomaly (the secretary hired from a Lamaze-class ad in 'Mr. Monk Fights City Hall', Crawford's odd phrasing 'No, she wouldn't be drinking now'), suddenly sees the one theory explaining all of them, and only afterwards manufactures shareable evidence for others. His absolute certainty, the chapter argues, rests on a metaphysical faith that only the true theory can explain every anomaly — a Leibnizian 'best of all possible ordered worlds' — the same obsession with order that makes him notice anomalies at all, though it makes him epistemically irresponsible by ordinary standards that weigh alternative hypotheses and simplicity.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin casts the creature as a modern Job: repeatedly and unreasonably mistreated by the De Laceys, the rustic whose child he saved, and Victor despite his benevolence, he cries 'This was then the reward of my benevolence!' - but unlike Job he loses faith, because his problem of evil is secular, justifying not 'the Ways of God to Man' but 'the Ways of Man to monsters.' The chapter traces the problem from Job and Paradise Lost through Bayle's defense of faith over reason and the Optimists' 'best of all possible worlds,' whose credibility drowned with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, setting Rousseau against Voltaire: Rousseau's Emile ('All is good leaving the hands of the author of things') demands that we make evil intelligible through self-knowledge, while Candide counsels tending our garden. The creature embodies Rousseau's line - 'I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend' - yet ends in self-abhorring remorse over Victor's death, leaving open whether self-knowledge can ever answer unreasonable suffering.

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This composite chapter opens with the volume's Introduction and then runs several essays. Jeff McLaughlin's 'What If?' reads DC's Crisis on Infinite Earths and Marvel's What If? series as literal illustrations of Leibniz's possible-worlds metaphysics: the multiverse of Earth-1, Earth-2 and the 3,000 doomed universes dramatizes counterfactuals and Leibniz's Theodicy argument (via the principle of sufficient reason) that God actualizes only the best of infinitely many possible worlds, with Descartes invoked on why a perfect God permits imperfection. Amy Kiste Nyberg's essay analyzes the 1954 Senate hearings on EC horror comics (Gaines's 'The Orphan') as an applied-ethics clash between publishers' free expression and protecting children, explicitly deploying Mill's On Liberty and harm principle to argue why the child-audience framing defeats the anti-censorship case. Stanford Carpenter's piece treats the Black Captain America (Truth: Red, White, and Black) as an epistemology-of-authorship problem.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 4. Acts of God
samples.relation: McCrossin reads Lecter's parable of the church collapses - 'It must feel good to God - He does it all the time, and are we not made in His image?' - as Lecter's solution to the problem of evil in both its theological (Job) and secular (Neiman) forms: a malevolent deity of the kind de Sade's Saint-Fond describes, doing God's work becomes Lecter's justification, and killing feels good because 'if one does what God does enough times, one will become as God is'. Following Neiman, he sets Rousseau's tradition (evil must be made intelligible - 'All is well leaving the hands of the author of things') against Voltaire's Candide refusal of theodicy, showing that Will and Starling live in Rousseau's camp except when facing Lecter himself, and that the Hannibal/Hannibal Rising revelation that Mischa's murder 'happened' to him radically revises his earlier claim that 'we don't invent our natures', with Starling's reason finally making 'a place for Mischa' in Lecter and Starling together.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Smith weighs Sheldon's vendetta against Wil Wheaton — the skipped 1995 Dixie Trek convention, the fake dead 'Nana' that won the Mystic Warlords tournament ('Game over, Moon Pie!'), the bowling-alley sabotage of Leonard and Penny — against theories of evil: Leibniz's best-of-all-possible-worlds theodicy (with Voltaire's Candide objection), Buber's claim that the lie is the specific evil humanity introduced into nature, and Arendt's banality of evil at Eichmann's trial, which shows Wil's deceptions are bad moral choices rather than evil. Nietzsche's will to power would instead admire Wil, and even Khan-style revenge, as proto-Übermensch exploitation. The chapter closes by reading Sheldon's 'Comic Book World paradigm' (the Green Goblin to his Spider-Man) through Ricoeur's view that evil is grasped through myths and symbols: Star Trek and comics are the symbolic framework by which he interprets wrongdoing he cannot otherwise fathom.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Voltaire Lives
samples.relation: Douglas Ficek traces The Onion's God stories — 'Lord Under Investigation For Failure To Provide,' God refusing to heal paralyzed little Timmy Yu, and 'God Cites Moving In Mysterious Ways' — back through Voltaire's Candide to Leibniz's theodicy, the 'best of all possible worlds' doctrine that Dr. Pangloss keeps reciting through hanging, slavery, and syphilis until Candide concludes we must cultivate our garden. The chapter's sharpest claim is that theodicy works by victim-blaming: Jerry Falwell's 9/11 rant earned the headline-only 'Jerry Falwell: Is That Guy A Dick Or What?' because he excused God by blaming secular Americans, just as Pastor Ellsworth blames heathen tsunami victims. Following theologian Dorothee Soelle, Ficek names this 'theological sadism,' and offers the Bible-drop missionaries of 'Poverty-Stricken Africans Receive Desperately Needed Bibles' as a modern Pangloss who mistakes moral obliviousness for grace.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: Time Enough to Drink the Poison
samples.relation: Domino reads 'The Veiled Lodger' as a drama about hope in a world after God: Holmes's 'Your life is not your own; keep your hands off it' revives Plato's Phaedo argument that we are the gods' possessions, but deist-or-atheist Mrs. Ronder is unmoved, so Holmes falls back on the Leibnizian alternative to the Stoic and Cartesian 'patience without hope' — the example of patient suffering as 'the most precious of all lessons,' grounded in Leibniz's hope that the world is no 'cruel jest.' Jefferson Hope's two pill boxes in A Study in Scarlet literalize the Leibnizian link between hope and divine justice by letting God choose who dies, while Trelawney Hope's gullibility makes the surname ironic. Mrs. Ronder's true hope was reunion with Leonardo, which his death destroyed; what saves her is a new hope founded on Watson's text, since only a writer ('I have made a slight change of name and place') can change the past.

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 6. Tris’s Compassion and the Problem of Evil
samples.relation: McCrossin reads Tris's whole arc as a struggle with the problem of evil, both the theological version from Job and the modern secular one Susan Neiman describes, in which unreasonable suffering threatens trust in human reason. He casts Tris as cut from Rousseau's mold - her insistence on making the evils of Jeanine, Marcus, and Evelyn intelligible - against Voltaire's Candide refusal to rationalize suffering, and treats the faction system as Rousseau's social-contract strategy for containing the inclination to evil while Tris herself plays a wartime Emile. The key is Tobias's lesson that selflessness and bravery are not that different: selflessness enables the courage that compassion motivates, from pressing her forehead to Jeanine's gun in the fear landscape to taking Caleb's place at the weapons lab, so that the trilogy ends with Tobias's 'we mend each other.'

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Matthew Watts sorts Fallout's artificial beings into cyborgs, synths, and pure robots and tests each against a theory of the self: Locke's memory theory explains the Robobrain socialites of Vault 118 and Nick Valentine's implanted prewar past, Parfit's psychological continuity (identity as a matter of degree) makes the Old World Blues Think Tank a caricature of a self stretched too thin, and Putnam's machine-table functionalism with multiple realizability (the Red Menace holotape running on any hardware) undermines Covenant's SAFE test by making function, not substrate, the mark of a mind. samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter argues Finn is not yet a true hero but is on a quest to become one: against rule systems like Mill's greatest-happiness utilitarianism and Kantian respect for persons, virtue ethics asks not 'what should I do' but 'who should I be', and Aristotle's point that children lack fully developed practical reason explains why Finn's good intentions misfire - removing Donny exposes the house people to Why-wolves, and Penny's trick humiliates him in the City of Thieves. Martha Nussbaum's ideal of every person as free and of equal dignity grounds heroism in the common good, and her work on literature and popular culture explains how watching Finn's exaggerated choices trains our own moral judgment. Citing Franco and Zimbardo's psychology of real heroes - empathy, risk tolerance, persistence - and closing with Seneca's 'how nobly you live', it concludes that since Aristotelian virtue is a habit, anyone can start by admitting they suck at heroism and practicing, as Jake's advice puts it.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: A Fork in the Road
samples.relation: Anderson contrasts two American freedoms through Springsteen and Tracy Chapman: the negative freedom of 'Racing in the Street,' 'Thunder Road,' and 'Born to Run' — Thoreauvian wildness, the outlaw who blows off duty, wins the dude from L.A.'s money and 'little girl' as a prize, then finds her crying on her daddy's porch — against the positive freedom of Chapman's 'Fast Car' heroine, who initially sees the fast car as a way to 'be someone' but finally sends the aimless drinker off and seeks empowerment of her own abilities. Drawing on Margaret Fuller (men squander freedom on appetite and domination), Charlotte Perkins Gilman (male-built structures channel women's freedom through men), and Nussbaum (flourishing, failure built into the structure), he argues that male negative freedom is dialectically coupled to women's oppression, that justice must trump the call of the wild, yet that men's own collateral damage — desolation, alienation — must also be addressed.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “There’s More to Life than Profit”
samples.relation: Held argues business ethics stalls because it begins from capitalism's presuppositions instead of asking what we fundamentally value, staging the impasse as Quark versus Rom and as Friedman's stockholder theory against Freeman's stakeholder theory ('The Dogs of War', Zek's reforms, 'Profit and Lace'). He recovers Aristotle's Politics distinction between economics serving the household's good and chrematistics — money-making as sheer accumulation, embodied in Quark's 'pure profit' embezzlement — and corrects the libertarian caricature of Adam Smith: the invisible hand works only within commutative justice and virtue, markets serving welfare rather than profit. Through Sen's capability approach and Quark's own defense of greed as promoting human development in 'Prophet Motive', the chapter concludes profit is only a means to freedom and well-being — 'there's more to life than profit' — and the Rules of Acquisition themselves must stand before the ethical judge.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Roger Hunt argues the films show that whoever assumes human superiority or ownership of created life gets eaten: Dieter Stark zaps a compy and is devoured by a swarm of them, Ludlow claims InGen's patent and becomes a hunting lesson for the baby T. rex. samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy

samples.title: Does the Piano Play Itself

samples.title: A Link to the Present
samples.relation: Compagno argues that the word 'I' in Zelda simultaneously names Link, the virtual body, and the player, the invisible will, and builds this into a 'Schopenhauerian Console': as Schopenhauer held, we have freedom of action but not freedom of will, since the decisions of the unknowable will never appear in consciousness (against Descartes' free mind and Dennett's Cartesian theater critique). Kant's transcendental subject, standing at the border of experience, becomes the player's perspective from which Hyrule exists, what Foucault would call an empirical-transcendental doublet. The payoff: Link's quest is fated and scripted, yet the player wills it in a perpetual present, enacting Schopenhauer's lesson that a determined life is still lived as one's own free act.

samples.title: A Link to the Present
samples.relation: Dario Compagno uses Schopenhauer's distinction between freedom of action and freedom of will — consciousness never witnesses the moment of decision, only hears the will's outcomes — to model the player-Link relation in Zelda. He proposes a 'Schopenhauerian Console' against Dennett's Cartesian theater: Link is the immanent virtual body in Hyrule, the player's will is the transcendent force outside it, and Kant's transcendental subject is the perspective on the border of experience that connects the two when the gamer becomes 'Link's player'. samples.title: Stable Bodies
samples.relation: Heinricy argues the human/Cylon line is drawn on the body: following Mary Douglas, bodies function as cultural boundaries, so Cylons figure as contamination to be hunted (Boomer in the fleet) and marked as other by violence (Gina's torture), though Athena's loyal service and Tigh's exposure show the fear is socially constructed rather than natural. Cylon insides are known only through technology (Caprica Six's glowing spine, Athena's blood interface in 'Flight of the Phoenix'), and their bodies' stability — no scars, aging, or change — is paid for in unstable minds (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer strangling Hera), whereas messy human bodies carry potential, hope, and change, as Apollo's weight fluctuation shows. Since we are all already cyborgs (vaccines, pills, GMOs), the Numbers are a further human-machine integration, and Hera and Nicky's blending is the ultimate 'contamination' and a new hope.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
samples.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Go Slowly
samples.relation: Wittkower frames In Rainbows' pay-what-you-want release with Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry: music is expressive communication awkwardly trapped in commodity form — even 'Happy Birthday' has an owner until 2030 — and digital distribution is finally tearing that frame down. His conclusion is that we must 'go slowly': listeners' rights to their culture outweigh labels' legitimate profit expectations, the way emancipation outweighed plantation business models, and labels must adapt into service providers rather than gatekeepers.

samples.title: Symbolism How We Create Meaning
samples.relation: DeHaven and Hendrickson read Columbia through Marx's class struggle: Comstock and Fink form the bourgeoisie controlling the means of production (Finkton, Handyman conversions of injured workers), while religion as 'opiate of the masses', the deified Founders, kinetoscope propaganda, and the Raffle keep the Shantytown proletariat in check. samples.title: 47. Snowpiercer as Philosophy The Danger to Humanity
samples.relation: Marquez 'pierces the veils' of Snowpiercer to argue the greatest danger to humanity is humanity itself. He reads Wilford's authoritarian, precisely population-controlled train through Plato's noble lie / myth of the metals (Mason's 'know your place'), Hobbes's social contract against a cannibalistic state of nature, and Machiavellian ends-justify-means to weigh whether Gilliam's secret compromise with Wilford is morally acceptable. samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
samples.relation: Hooke reads Serling's ambivalence toward the State through 'The Obsolete Man,' where librarian Romney Wordsworth is condemned as obsolete and reads Psalm 23 to mock the Chancellor — analyzed via Foucault's shepherd-flock model of power and its paradox, which 'The Shelter' restages as neighbors deciding who gets inside. He then maps the Rawls–Nozick dispute: whether a state just enough to enforce equal rights and the difference principle must inevitably invade personal freedom (Nozick's Jerry West self-respect example), with both agreeing that no state squashing dignity and freedom is just. Under a Nietzsche epigraph on the gods' laughter, Wordsworth's smile before death becomes the indefinable freedom of laughing at obsolete authority — the unnamed Zone, running from Socrates and Heraclitus to Serling.

samples.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
samples.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
samples.relation: Hooke stages the liberalism-versus-libertarianism dispute through Serling's ambivalence about the State: Foucault's shepherd-flock model from his Security, Territory, Population lectures fails as politics, since 'The Shelter' shows the shepherd deciding who stays and who goes ends in mob violence, and in 'The Obsolete Man' librarian Romney Wordsworth reads Psalm 23 to a State that has declared God and books obsolete. The Rawls-Nozick quarrel (justice as fairness and the difference principle against Nozick's minimal state and his basketball-shooter case for keeping self-respect out of politics) frames how much State freedom requires. Wordsworth's laugh before his execution, under Nietzsche's epigraph about gods who mock, embodies the undefinable freedom no State can name.

samples.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
samples.title: The Politics of Difference
samples.relation: Debra Jackson argues that despite its ethnic and gender stereotypes the Warcraft universe is structurally a Rawlsian liberal utopia: designers choose class balance behind a veil of ignorance, racial traits are symmetric, professions are open to all, and a difference principle guarantees even the most disadvantaged player a decent experience. Plato's Republic supplies the gender argument — as Plato made the soul rather than reproductive function the criterion for guardians, WoW makes gender irrelevant to gameplay. Yet players import real-world prejudice (anti-Gnome hate speech, female toons shunted into healer roles, mocked male Blood Elves), so structural equality never yields substantial equality: WoW is sexist and racist because we are.

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
samples.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Tilting at Windmills
samples.relation: Reads Protogen through Horkheimer and Adorno's Dialectic of Enlightenment: like Odysseus tied to the mast while his sailors take the wax, Dresden's team had empathy surgically removed ('we modified our science team to remove ethical restraints'), Mao weeps at Julie's protomolecule corpse yet calls her death 'lucky', and Strickland experiments on Katoa and Mei Meng — self-made monsters serving the Baconian dream of conquering nature (New Atlantis, witch-trial language of 'penetrating her holes and corners'). Via Maria Mies and Carolyn Merchant's ecofeminism, it traces this domination of nature to pastoralist castration and the control of women's reproduction, culminating in Marco's theft of Filip and 'She left us. She left us both' — Naomi cast as nature to be mastered. Against them, Holden's childhood on the family farm, a cooperative 'let grow and make grow' world, is why Avasarala cannot play him and why he withholds broadcasts at Ilus: he is a knight who wants everyone to grow and speak for themselves, not to conquer.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Mirror, Mirror
samples.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
samples.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves. The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 11 Beastly Boys The Racial-Sexual Politics of Meat
samples.relation: Huerter reads M'Baku's 'I'm kidding. We are vegetarians' punchline through Carol Adams's sexual politics of meat and bell hooks's plantation patriarchy: since colonial meat-eating signified masculine mastery over nature (Plumwood's reason/nature dualism) while enslaved people were fed plant foods and cast as edible themselves, audiences primed by the racist cannibal trope expect M'Baku to be a savage, so his refusal of flesh turns the colonizer's gaze back on itself. Killmonger, by contrast, embodies the Black patriarchy produced by the American military-industrial complex ('He's one of ours'), a plantation patriarch whose hypermasculine conquest — killing Linda, burning the Herb garden, his defiant 'death was better than bondage' exit — replays colonial violence even in liberation's name, against which M'Baku's warrior-but-vegetarian politics marks a moral asymmetry.

samples.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
samples.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Aleman, an ethnobotanist, asks 'Is coffee green?' and unpacks the many senses of 'green' (raw bean, naïve, money, and ecologically friendly) before weighing coffee's growth, organic and shade-grown methods, fair trade, globalization, and value chain. She judges coffee greenest at the source (shade-grown farms preserve migrating-bird habitat) but least green in the fossil-fueled journey from Global South farm to Global North cup, invoking Vandana Shiva's claim that 'drinking coffee is a political act' and Rigoberta Menchú on coffee and indigenous survival. She concludes the answer is partly subjective—withholding final judgment while resolving to keep drinking fair-trade, organic, shade-grown, single-source coffee—and warns of the cognitive dissonance, mirroring oil dependence, between judging coffee ungreen and drinking it anyway.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
samples.relation: Eberl weighs genetic enhancement and cloning through Trek's test cases: Julian Bashir's parents' enhancement leaves him feeling 'a fraud' ('You used to be my father. Now, you're my architect'), the Moab IV 'Masterpiece Society' breeds out 'the unknown, self-discovery, things that make life worth living', and the Jem'Hadar show desire itself engineered for control. He argues the right to an open future constrains designing children (B'Elanna's wish to de-Klingonize her baby, Worf pressuring Alexander), defends genetic treatment while rejecting genetic determinism, and uses Kass and Rovane with Picard and Shinzon, the Mariposa clones, and Trip's clone Sim to show clones are numerically distinct persons. Against Malik's Augments quoting Nietzsche — 'mankind is something to be surpassed' — the chapter argues the Übermensch demands self-mastery through philosophy, not eugenic engineering, tracing eugenics from Plato's Guardian breeding scheme through Buck v. Bell to modern prenatal selection.

samples.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
samples.title: 8. Night of the Living Disabled
samples.relation: Reads Constance's treatment of Addy and Beau Langdon through the eugenic roots of the horror genre (Angela Smith's Hideous Progeny, The Black Stork, the Production Code): outward bodily difference assumed to prove inner defect, and the disabled treated as better off dead - Addy finding peace only as 'a pretty girl at last' after death, Beau suffocated in the attic. Against the medical model the chapter defends Alison Kafer's political-relational model and crip futurity (Tate's 'He only suffered because of you'), arguing that ableism, not disability itself, makes their lives unlivable and that imagining disabled futures differently is a matter of survival.

samples.title: Chapter 12 - Grow, My Dears, the Eugenicist Said
samples.relation: Opens the eugenics part with Flow My Tears' Jason Taverner — a beautiful, charismatic, fast-healing 'six' from an abandoned government breeding program, 'not a Nexus-Six, but not unlike one either.' Defining eugenics through the dog-and-wolf contrast in selective breeding, it notes that the 'eu' (good) in eugenics smuggles in an ethical judgment, and poses the part's driving question: who decides what counts as a 'good' or 'bad' trait, and by what right?

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: What Was on Wittgenstein’s iPod
samples.relation: Rehn argues there is no essential definition of the iPod: Shuffle, Nano, Classic, and Touch share only overlapping, criss-crossing similarities, exactly as Wittgenstein's family resemblance handles 'sport' (water polo vs. boxing) and 'game.' Even Cover Flow -- a physically impossible floating cascade of albums -- feels instantly familiar, showing familiarity is something users construct from hints rather than perceive, and syncing, playlists, and the Music Quiz game endlessly re-manufacture it (the iPod as the new McDonald's golden arches abroad). Flipping the relation via Actor-Network Theory, he notes the iPod tracks play counts, pushes 'Listeners Also Bought,' and trains our flicking gestures, so that perhaps the iPod becomes familiar with us; the Microsoft Zune figures as the abject, zombie-like copy whose perverse familiarity reveals a politics of recognition, and the closing game of imagining Wittgenstein's playlist endorses natural language's many language games over exact definitions.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
