samples.relation: Vaclavik follows Lyra's career as liar and trickster, from the Silvertongue performance that goads Iofur Raknison into fighting Iorek Byrnison, up to the reversal in the Land of the Dead where the harpy screams 'Liar!' and only true stories can feed the ghosts. She frames Lyra's boast that she is the best liar there ever was yet is not lying as a version of the Liar Paradox, then dissolves the puzzle by showing that lies continue after the katabasis (Will's comforting fib, Mrs. Coulter's noble treachery with Metatron) just as truth-telling appeared before it. Truth triumphs in the underworld not for its own sake but because it suits the audience: the dead need the world they have lost, so storytelling, truthful or invented, is judged by what it does for its listeners.

samples.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Cook and Kellen formalize two rules of the golden lasso (the bound must answer, and must say what they believe true) and derive the Paradox of the Golden Lasso - 'Will your answer to this question be no?' - as a Liar Paradox variant, complete with a Revenge version that survives allowing 'maybe' as an answer. Bizarra's opposite-speaking lasso generates knights-and-knaves puzzles in the Smullyan style, a Wonder Woman/Bizarra/Harley Quinn variant of Boolos's Hardest Logic Puzzle Ever, and solutions exploiting what the bound believe rather than say. They end by using Bizarro #1 snapping the lasso and the Queen of Fables' huntsman doing the same to illustrate objective truth and the philosophy of fiction - what is fictionally true of characters who do not literally exist.

name: Purity and Danger (dirt as matter out of place)

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: Stable Bodies
samples.relation: Heinricy argues the one clear human-Cylon difference is the body, analyzed through Mary Douglas's account of bodies as culturally invented boundaries: Cylons are feared as 'contamination' of the fleet (Boomer's body, segregated like Jim Crow bodies), and Gina Six's torture and rape mark her body as out-of-place other even as her human-looking blood and wounds undermine the boundary. She contrasts messy, changing human bodies (Apollo's weight fluctuation, aging, scars as records of experience) with stable, disposable Cylon bodies that never mark learning, arguing human change yields potential and hope while Cylon bodily stability may cost mental stability (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer attacking Hera). Cyborg theory then collapses the boundary (we are all cyborgs via vaccines and prosthetics, Cylons merely more integrated, the Hybrid a warning of over-integration), leaving Hera and Nicky as the 'ultimate contamination' that blends the two.

samples.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
samples.title: Stable Bodies
samples.relation: Heinricy argues the human/Cylon line is drawn on the body: following Mary Douglas, bodies function as cultural boundaries, so Cylons figure as contamination to be hunted (Boomer in the fleet) and marked as other by violence (Gina's torture), though Athena's loyal service and Tigh's exposure show the fear is socially constructed rather than natural. Cylon insides are known only through technology (Caprica Six's glowing spine, Athena's blood interface in 'Flight of the Phoenix'), and their bodies' stability — no scars, aging, or change — is paid for in unstable minds (Tigh killing Ellen, Boomer strangling Hera), whereas messy human bodies carry potential, hope, and change, as Apollo's weight fluctuation shows. Since we are all already cyborgs (vaccines, pills, GMOs), the Numbers are a further human-machine integration, and Hera and Nicky's blending is the ultimate 'contamination' and a new hope.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Shaman, Heal Thyself
samples.relation: Culver reads Monk as a shamanic figure in Arnold van Gennep's and Victor Turner's sense: a liminal man, neither cop nor civilian, fixed in the transitional stage of mourning Trudy, who heals society's disorder from its margins as Holmes and Poirot did. Drawing on Mary Douglas's Purity and Danger (dirt as defilement and disorder), she interprets Monk's ritualized gestures and utterances, framing the scene with his hands, the rare solving-smile, 'he's the guy' and 'Here's what happened', as the ceremonial performance by which disorder is overcome. Episodes like 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' and 'Mr. Monk Joins a Cult' then show the shaman's bind: whenever Monk attains purity or happiness he loses his sacred gift, so he must refuse to heal himself and remain 'a blessing and a curse'.

samples.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
samples.title: Futurama and Philosophy
samples.relation: Oschman reads 'Godfellas' as an answer to the problem of evil: Bender, made god of the Shrimpkins, destroys them by meddling too much, and the God Entity explains 'if you do too much, people get dependent. And if you do nothing, they lose hope.' After testing the contrast response (pain makes Slurm sweet) and the Free Will Defense (which covers moral evils like the returning garbage ball of 'A Big Piece of Garbage' but not natural evils or the taste of anchovies), the chapter adopts John Hick's soul-making theodicy: God's epistemic distance - compared to Fry's obsession after tasting super Slurm - keeps creatures uncompelled so they can grow into free moral agents. Fry's slow evolution from delivery boy to 'slightly less lazy slob' is soul-making, and 'The Late Philip J. Fry' wryly confirms life's purpose is 'probably some hogwash about the human spirit.'

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: Redemption
samples.relation: Stephen Bilynskyj tests John Hick's soul-making theodicy—that God allows suffering because virtues like courage, temperance, and compassion need pain to form—against Cash's life and songs. Using Aristotle on habituation by pleasure and pain (Cash's first amphetamine euphoria and the ostrich-attack painkillers as missed occasions for temperance) and Aquinas on innate aptitude and divinely infused virtue, he argues virtue can form without suffering (by genes or miracle), so soul-making alone cannot justify evil, as Cash himself implies about his mother's grief after Jack's death. Cash instead locates redemption in Christ's suffering ('Redemption,' 'Why Me, Lord?'), while the intervention by his son John Carter shows pain still occasioning real growth in temperance.

samples.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
samples.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
samples.relation: Haas uses Dean's stubborn refusal to believe in God, even after meeting Castiel, escaping Hell, and visiting Heaven, to run through the problem of evil. Casey's challenge in 'Sin City' states the logical problem; the free-will theodicy answers it but falters before Supernatural's designed horrors like the rugaru, a creature God built to suffer an irresistible hunger that ends with it eating its spouse. Dean's real objection is the evidential problem, that the amount and severity of apparently pointless evil makes the omni-God unlikely, and neither a 'natural order' defense (Dick Roman humanely farming humans for food) nor John Hick's soul-making theodicy explains suffering far beyond what character formation requires.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “All Good Things Must Come to an End”
samples.relation: Thorsrud casts Spock and Data's exchange in 'Unification, Part II' — Spock dispassionate by choice, Data longing for emotion — as a replay of the ancient debate between Stoics and Peripatetics over whether to eliminate or moderate the passions. The Aristotelian side is built from Data's emotion-chip rage while killing a Borg ('Descent'), his unfelt breakup with Jenna ('In Theory'), and Riker's defense of trust after Ishara's betrayal ('Legacy'): emotions are judgments with pleasure or pain, there is a right amount to feel, and invulnerability costs the 'emotional bonds that make us who we are.' The Stoic reply uses Epictetus's distinction between involuntary impressions and assent (Picard's fear on the Borg ship vs. the holodeck), Cicero's refusal to 'moderate' what is simply a fault, and Seneca on anger, exemplified by Spock's 'quite logical relief' in 'Amok Time', his calculated desperation in 'The Galileo Seven', and his saving the bigot Stiles in 'Balance of Terror' — leaving the Peripatetic conclusion that fortune's goods are not mere indifferents and we may rightly 'smile with so little provocation.'

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
samples.relation: Mills reads Mr. Bates, the lame, twice-imprisoned, uncomplaining valet, as Downton's Epictetus, using him and the household to teach the Stoic dichotomy of control: only our judgments, desires, and actions are up to us, while jobs, reputations, and inheritances (Thomas's coveted valet post, Mary's scandal, Molesley's flower cup) are 'preferred indifferents' to be pursued without enslavement. Death figures as the great rejected indifferent, handled through Pamuk's demise and Mrs. Hughes's calm 'One day, I will die' upon finding a lump, as well as the grief of Isobel and Mary over Matthew. The closing section turns to Hierocles's concentric circles, with Sybil helping Gwen and Carson comforting Mary as drawing outsiders into the inner circle, a Stoic cosmopolitanism that Thomas, who sees the Crawleys as mere employers, fails entirely. The Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves' serves as the chapter's Stoic motto.

samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: Re-examining 'The Enchiridion!' trial by trial - the gnome illusions, the ogre whose dollar Finn steals and then returns, the dark mage's brain world, the wallop given the Key-per in devil pajamas - the chapter argues Finn wins the hero's handbook without being righteous: he is brave, tender and ingenious, but gullible, hasty and violent, slaying whatever he is told is evil and running from the gnome test. Epictetus's Stoic Enchiridion supplies the standard the show's book lacks: only virtue matters, wealth, fame and comfort are indifferents, and a real handbook teaches how to lose, age and admit mistakes, not just how to win, which is exactly what Billy's quit-heroism shows Ooo's greatest hero never learned. Because bravery without good judgment could as easily serve a Nazi, a terrorist or the Lich, Finn's lack of practical wisdom means the 'most righteous hero' in Ooo is an impetuous boy - proof of how morally broken the Land of Ooo is.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 6. Keeping It under Control
samples.relation: Mills presents Bates - lame leg, repeated prison spells, the public fall when O'Brien kicks his cane - as an Epictetan Stoic who 'manages' misfortune by confining his concern to what he controls, echoing the Dowager's 'I hope we're in control of something, if only ourselves.' The chapter explains the dichotomy of control and preferred indifferents through Thomas's enslaved pursuit of the valet post, O'Brien's soap-on-the-floor scheme, Mary's panicked engagement to Richard Carlisle, and Mrs. Hughes's proportioning of her cancer scare, and treats death as the great rejected indifferent via Pamuk, Sybil, and Matthew. It closes with Hierocles' concentric circles: the household's best moments (Sybil helping Gwen, the staff rallying to free Bates) collapse upstairs and downstairs into one family, while Thomas's closed inner circle marks his failure of Stoic virtue.

samples.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Hummel maps the Jedi Order onto Epictetus's Stoicism: philosophy as a way of life, virtue through wisdom, the dichotomy of control ('some things are up to us'), and treating outcomes like flying or other people's fates as preferred indifferents within the will of the Force. Anakin falls because he misconceives power as the ability to do amazing things - stopping people from dying - instead of mastery of his own judgments, and he refuses Stoic indifference toward Shmi and Padme. The chapter also indicts the Jedi's own un-Stoic lapses: mind tricks on Watto, entering the Clone Wars, and Mace Windu's attempt to execute a subdued Sidious.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Group Will
samples.relation: Testerman argues the film's heist is ironic because nobody in it acts from conscious will: citing Libet's readiness-potential experiments and Penfield's stimulation cases, she claims the feeling of willing is a post-hoc 'epistemic illusion,' so Fischer's inception merely dramatizes what happens all the time — Cobb's 'all experience is inception' becomes a thesis about ordinary agency, with Spinoza's dictum that freedom is ignorance of the causes of our actions as its motto. She reads the plot through this lens: Saito's unexamined hunger for power silently drives the team's 'group will,' Cobb's 'positive emotion trumps negative emotion' tactic exploits the limbic system, and cheaper tricks (Arthur's elephant, foot-in-the-door, subliminal advertising) would have worked as well. Against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly livable, since introspection can never reach the subconscious causes of behavior.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: Group Will
samples.relation: Testerman turns inception against itself: Cobb and Saito believe they freely plan the Fischer job, but conscious will is a feeling, not a cause. From William James's effortful attention and Dewey's willpower she moves to Penfield's stimulated patients and Libet's readiness-potential experiments showing the brain prepares action before we feel we will it, so Fischer, Cobb and Saito are all equally 'incepted' by subconscious forces - 'freedom is ignorance of the causes of actions', as she glosses Spinoza, with Hume's point that causality is only inferred. Advertising, the foot-in-the-door effect and subliminal primes already do inception's work more cheaply, and the team's 'group will' flows from Saito's own unexamined drive for power, so against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly suitable for living.

samples.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
samples.title: The Instructive Impossibility of Being John Malkovich
samples.relation: Hagberg treats Being John Malkovich as a refutation of the dualist fantasy that one could achieve transparent knowledge of another mind by occupying it. Through the film's four levels—Schwartz as spectator inside Malkovich, Lotte's transgender re-embodiment, Schwartz's puppeteering, and Malkovich falling into his own portal to the 'Malkovich, Malkovich' hell—he shows, via Jamesian relational sensation and Wittgenstein's private-language argument, that it is always still Schwartz who senses, so no one ever becomes Malkovich. The self-enclosed Malkovich world, where everyone can only say 'Malkovich,' dramatizes that selfhood is relationally emergent (Royce, Mead) and that experience is inviolably one's own (Margalit on remembered emotion).

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: All Human Experience is an Impression
samples.relation: Ruetenik argues the best SNL impressions are not 'spot on': Carvey's Bush ('Not gonna do it. Wouldn't be prudent') and the Tom Brokaw pre-tapes sketch created new experiences rather than faithful copies, while Darrell Hammond's exact impressions made him a 'tribute band' without Carvey's artistry. Dewey's Art as Experience and James's selective attention, in which every perceiver is an impressionist ignoring the blooming buzzing confusion, ground the claim that all experience is creative re-presentation rather than tribute to reality. He then turns the point political: SNL casting Amy Poehler over a spot-on Black impressionist as Michael Jackson tells us something about the audience's own selective, and possibly racist, experience.

samples.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
samples.title: Foreword
samples.relation: Show writer David Weddle recounts how Ron Moore pushed him and Brad Thompson to abandon Star Trek-style expository dialogue and tell 'Act of Contrition' through flashbacks interleaved with the present, dramatizing Starbuck's guilt over passing Zak Adama on his flight test. He argues this unlocked a stream-of-consciousness mode — dreams, hallucinations, and memories flowing out of characters' inner emotional lives — that the series extended in episodes like 'Scar,' 'Maelstrom,' and 'Unfinished Business,' echoing Faulkner's 'the past isn't even past.' The foreword is a creator's testimony that BSG's scrambled-chronology storytelling is what made the show worthy of a book of philosophical readings.

samples.book: 281 - Cannabis – Philosophy for Everyone - What Were We Just Talking About_
samples.title: Cannabis Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Hathaway and Sharpley analyze the cannabis experience of medical-'compassion club' users through Csikszentmihalyi's concept of 'flow.' They ground flow in William James's 'stream of consciousness' and in Taoism, reading Tao as 'a patterned flow of the universe' and wu wei as the effortless equilibrium users describe ('it just centers me,' 'I take an inventory on my soul'). Against Western monophasic medicine, they defend users' 'anecdotal' testimony as legitimate knowledge of a body–mind–spirit balance that cannabis restores.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: The Loneliest Witch
samples.relation: Auxier gives three theories of why water melts the Wicked Witch, one for each register of Oz: as dream (Bergson's account of dreams as memory explains the fire/water effect-swap), as Baum's fairytale (Susanne Langer's presentational symbols make dryness-wickedness versus water-as-life the tale's moral physics), and as Gregory Maguire's possible world, where the philosophy of language takes over. He narrates Frege's sense/reference distinction—mayor of the Munchkins—to explain how fiction can support truth and falsity ('Dorothy melts the Witch' true, 'Dorothy tried to melt her' false), then deploys Putnam's Twin Earth thought experiment: 'water' in Oz is XYZ while Kansas water is H2O, so Elphaba's word 'water' does not mean what Dorothy's does, and meanings just aren't in the head. Elphaba—the unique being straddling two worlds, killed by H2O she cannot name and terrified by dreams of oceans—is offered as an even stronger argument for Putnam's semantic externalism than Twin Earth's molecule-for-molecule doppelgangers.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

samples.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
samples.title: 3. The M. Night Sh-imulation Hypothesis
samples.relation: The chapter runs Bostrom's simulation argument against 'M. Night Shaym-Aliens!', where the Zigerions trap Rick in simulations-within-simulations to steal his concentrated dark matter formula, and reads their cheap shortcuts ('My man!' NPCs, human music, Jerry's Appley award) as the glitches and shadow-people Bostrom predicts. It presses the epistemological problem that any evidence for the simulation equally supports its denial, an underdetermination that devastates the theory, and traces the lineage of 'the real world isn't real' through Plato's summoners and allegory of the cave, Descartes's dream doubt, and Paley's design analogy (Morty as the beautiful machine), ending with the microverse battery of 'The Ricks Must Be Crazy': this is the universe we live in, so get used to it.

samples.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
samples.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
samples.relation: Johnson argues that because Zelda has no single authorial vision (teams, outside developers, cryptic Aonuma interviews), the timeline is a 'communication game' fans play together. Interpretation follows the hermeneutic circle of Heidegger and Gadamer (parts inform the whole, as when Wind Waker's references to Ganon's earlier attacks make sense of the series), faces Leibnizian underdetermination since infinitely many theories fit the games, and uses Ockham's razor, whose failures (the y=2x formula) show that simplicity is relative to a community's training, as in Wittgenstein's pupil who suddenly counts '1,004, 1,008'. Hence Miyamoto's own claim that Zelda is a communication game: designers supply puzzle pieces, and the fan community creates the meaning.

samples.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
samples.title: Zelda Is a Communication Game!
samples.relation: Carl Matthew Johnson argues that the split-timeline versus linear-timeline fan war, settled by Eiji Aonuma's 2006 Nintendo Dream interview, is really a hermeneutic meta-game fans play on top of Zelda. He applies the Heidegger-Gadamer hermeneutic circle — the Ganon references in Wind Waker make sense only from knowledge of the whole series, while gossip-stone text about Kaepora Gaebora feeds back into the whole — then uses Leibniz's curve-fitting problem to show timeline evidence underdetermines any single interpretation. Ockham's razor and Wittgenstein's counting-by-twos rule-following example reveal that simplicity is community-relative, culminating in Miyamoto's 2007 claim that Zelda was designed from the start as a 'communication game' among players.

name: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Conclusion Whatever I Goddamn Like
samples.relation: S. W. Sondheimer argues that Avasarala's election loss to Nancy Gao is explained not by competence but by millennia of gender expectations. She excavates the lineage: Aristotle's form/matter hierarchy ('matter yearns for form as the female for the male', women as incomplete 'deformed males' with 'fewer teeth') used to bar women from politics, Hume's portrait of women as near-livestock incapable of the sublime, and Romantic-era bodily confinement — mapping each onto Avasarala's staff recasting her as a 'nurturing, caring family matriarch', her forced public apology for the failed Inaros boarding raid that a male commander like Errinwright would never have had to make, and Arjun seizing control of the narrative of their son Charanpal's death. Closing the loop with the 2016 US election (Clinton versus Trump), the chapter argues that even in 2350 voters punish the 'nasty woman' and reward the comfortable mold Gao fits, and demands we 'dig this garbage philosophy out of our shared consciousness and set it on fire.'

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Gutwald takes seven-year-old Charlotte Benjamin's viral letter ('all the girls did was sit at home, go to the beach, and shop... but the boys went on adventures, worked, saved people') to argue the LEGO Friends theme is Wollstonecraftian 'friendly sexism' — revering girls as pretty play-things in a house-bound Heartlake City rather than oppressing them outright. Following Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes a woman' and her point that men describe the world from their own perspective, plus Mill's Subjection of Women observation that argument alone cannot beat a 'mass of feeling', she explains how pinkified toy segregation feeds implicit bias, schemas, and stereotype threat in both girls and boys. Her fix is structural: make Friends bricks and mini-dolls compatible with the rest of the system ('Let the Friends go to Space!') and return to the gender-neutral 1981 'What it is is beautiful' ad.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: “Happily Ever After, Now and Then”
samples.relation: Erin McKenna explains how a feminist can love Buffett by reading 'Fins' and 'Why Don't We Get Drunk (and Screw)' as critiques of predatory land sharks rather than endorsements, and 'Margaritaville' as a man admitting 'it's my own damn fault.' Against Rousseau's pliable helpmate ideal of woman she sets Wollstonecraft's Vindication — equal education and personhood for women — and Charlotte Perkins Gilman's pragmatist-feminist case that women's economic, physical, and mental dependence stunts everyone. Buffett's novels then pass the Gilman test: Desdemona, Trevor Kane, Cleopatra Highbourne, and Sophie are smart, independent women, and the male leads must reform their habits to earn them, aiming at Desdemona's 'happily ever after, now and then' instead of the fairy-tale ending.

samples.book: 264 - Jane Austen and Philosophy
samples.title: Jane Austen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Dashwood examines women owning property in Austen, arguing the 'great ladies' (Lady Catherine, Mrs. Ferrars, Lady Denham) are drawn as despotic, avaricious, and negligent managers not because they are women but because a deficient female education left them unfit, echoing Wollstonecraft's Vindication that female failings are constructed by upbringing. She contrasts them with propertyless heroines who show the reason and moral principle to manage estates well. Emma is the pivotal case: as the one female proprietor at a novel's center, she risks becoming a tyrannical great lady but, guided by her superior education and Knightley's example at Donwell, develops the social conscience needed for ethical ownership.

samples.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
samples.title: Heteronormative horrors
samples.relation: Reading virgins and the vagina dentata as the dyad through which horror polices female sexuality, the chapter uses Irigaray's account of the virgin as prop to male subjectivity and Creed's femme castratrice to analyse Halloween's 'Final Girl', Teeth's toothed-vagina revenge on abstinence-only purity culture, Jennifer's Body and Haute Tension. It closes with Rich's 'compulsory heterosexuality' and Wittig's 'heterosexual contract' to argue horror naturalises heteronormativity by casting female sexuality as either contained (virgin) or monstrously open (vagina dentata).

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: George Dunn tests Katniss's luck-saturated life against Kant's claim that the good will shines 'like a jewel' regardless of fortune, with Peeta's vow to 'die as myself' as the stronghold the Gamemakers cannot touch, and with Seneca's dictum that what Fortune has not given she cannot take away. He then runs Nagel's four kinds of moral luck through the trilogy: Haymitch's reaping-made alcoholism as constitutive luck, Rue's death sparing Katniss an impossible final choice as circumstantial luck, Peeta's rooftop words echoing unconsciously behind the flowers for Rue as causal luck, and the revolution's success as resultant luck without which Katniss would have been the destroyer of District 12 rather than its torchbearer. Framing the Gamemakers as Fortuna on her wheel, he ends with the berries: since Katniss can never untangle whether she held them out from love, defiance, or self-protection, even moral worth proves hostage to luck and to the opacity of our own motives.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: “Livin’ and Dyin’ in Three-Quarter Time”
samples.relation: Randall Auxier uses Buffett's catalog to think about fortune and fate, reading Buffett's bold career moves (walking out on Nashville for the beach, later annexing it via 'It's Five o'Clock Somewhere') through Machiavelli's advice to marry Fortuna and master her tricks with virtù. Against Aristotle's demanding answer that only aretē, moral excellence, defends happiness against bad luck, he takes Vico's middle path: natural causes, moral causes, and the occasions of fortune are gathered under providence, so Buffett's seaplane crash ('God, Buddha, St. Christopher, my guardian angel... luck, and the United States Navy water-survival training') shows any fate can be turned to good ends for others. Sorting Buffett's songs into places, times, meetings, sentiments, and thoughts — the key sentiment being the wistful — the chapter lands on contentment as gratitude: being 'livin' and dyin' in three-quarter time.'

samples.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
samples.title: The Devil and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads Tolkien's Silmarillion through Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy: elves, being artists, understand Melkor not as tempter but as bad artist, from his rebellious solo in the Music of the Ainur to his botched sub-creations - orcs bred from kidnapped elves - and his covetous collecting of the silmarils. Boethius supplies the machinery: evil seeks a good by unnatural means and only approximates it, wickedness debases its practitioner into a beast, God's foreknowledge embraces free choices without causing them, and Providence is a spinning disc at whose center alone one is steady - so Melkor's rebellion leaves him less free, dragged around the rim. Tolkien's contrast between art (for beauty) and magic (for control) explains why the Devil can only mimic creation, never make anything real.
